bio: I am an undergraduate psychology researcher at Ashoka University, minoring in biology and philosophy. I work on questions about attention and inhibitory control, and about how early emotional experiences shape later psychological functioning.

Most of my work is experimental and quantitative: reaction-time paradigms, questionnaire research, and eye-tracking. I have worked in developmental psychopathology, clinical psychology and comparative cognition, in labs at Ashoka University and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
I am an undergraduate at Ashoka University (CGPA 3.86/4, Major GPA 3.95/4) and spent a semester on exchange at UNC Chapel Hill. I intend to pursue graduate study in cognitive or clinical psychology.

goals: My undergraduate thesis asks whether childhood emotional abuse and emotional neglect relate differently to inhibitory control in emerging adults. Alongside it, I am building experience in both laboratory experimentation and clinical assessment, because I want to keep working at the point where cognitive methods and mental health questions meet.
